skill.name: security-scanning-security-dependencies
skill.description: Scan dependencies across npm, Python, Go, and Rust projects, prioritize vulnerabilities, generate SBOM data, and plan tested remediation.
skill.summary: Audit multi-ecosystem dependencies and produce prioritized remediation guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All 22 static findings are false positives caused by fixed-argument scanner commands, ordinary Python loops, shell syntax, Markdown formatting, and safety guidance. Contextual review found unpinned scanner installations and CI error suppression that can weaken scan integrity.

remediation.issue: Scanner installation examples use unpinned package versions and @latest.
remediation.suggestion: Pin scanner versions and hashes, document trusted registries, and review version updates before changing CI.

remediation.issue: Several CI scan commands suppress failures with || true.
remediation.suggestion: Capture scanner exit status separately, fail on execution or parsing errors, and parse reports structurally before enforcing severity thresholds.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Security Tool Installation
semantic_findings.description: The playbook installs scanners without pinned versions and uses @latest. Unexpected or compromised releases could enter CI and local environments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited commands explicitly install unversioned packages and govulncheck@latest. This is a direct supply-chain reproducibility risk.

semantic_findings.title: Suppressed Scanner Failures Can Produce False Assurance
semantic_findings.description: Several CI commands ignore scanner failures. Missing or malformed reports can bypass the later text count and allow an incomplete scan to pass.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly applies || true to scan commands and checks only matched output text afterward. Scanner errors are not distinguished from clean results.

content.value_statement: Dependency risks are difficult to compare across package ecosystems. This skill organizes scanner results, prioritizes findings, and prepares practical remediation and reporting guidance.
actual_capabilities: Detects npm, Python, Go, and Rust dependency manifests.
Shows fixed-argument scanner integrations for four package ecosystems.
Normalizes vulnerability findings into shared severity and package fields.
Prioritizes findings using severity, exploit availability, and available fixes.
Generates CycloneDX-style component data, Markdown summaries, and SARIF results.
Provides CI scanning and staged dependency update examples.
limitations: Requires compatible manifests, scanner tools, and network access to vulnerability databases.
Examples need adaptation and testing before production use.
Generated SBOM logic includes vulnerable components, not every installed dependency.
Scanner results can contain false positives, stale advisories, or ecosystem-specific gaps.

use_cases.title: Audit a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Review changed lockfiles, identify newly introduced vulnerabilities, and propose verified package updates.

use_cases.title: Standardize CI Scanning
use_cases.description: Create consistent dependency checks and severity gates across repositories with different package ecosystems.

use_cases.title: Prepare Supply Chain Evidence
use_cases.description: Produce vulnerability summaries and SBOM guidance for release reviews and compliance evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Scan One Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this repository's dependency manifests. Identify the ecosystems, recommend read-only scanners, and summarize vulnerabilities without changing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single repository

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these dependency scan results. Rank remediation by severity, exploitability, runtime exposure, fix availability, and likely upgrade impact.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Safe Remediation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a staged remediation plan for these vulnerable packages. Separate low-risk patches from breaking upgrades and define tests and rollback checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multi-Ecosystem CI
prompt_templates.prompt: Design dependency scanning for npm, Python, Go, and Rust. Pin tools, preserve reports, detect scanner failures, and enforce configurable severity policies.

output_examples.input: Review an npm project with two high findings and one available patch.
output: Summary: Two high-severity findings affect production dependencies.
Priority: Apply the compatible patch first, then rerun tests and npm audit.
Verification: Confirm the lockfile changed only expected packages.

output_examples.input: Create a remediation plan for Python and Go scan results.
output: Immediate: Address reachable critical and high findings with available fixes.
Planned: Test transitive upgrades in isolated branches.
Deferred: Document accepted risks with owners and review dates.

output_examples.input: Summarize dependency scan evidence for a release review.
output_examples.output: The release report lists affected packages, advisory identifiers, severity, available fixes, accepted risks, and the date of the latest successful scan.

best_practices: Run read-only scans before proposing dependency changes.
Pin scanner versions and verify tool installation sources.
Test updates and preserve reports for comparison and rollback.
anti_patterns: Do not apply automatic fixes without explicit approval.
Do not treat scanner errors or missing reports as clean results.
Do not prioritize only by severity without checking exposure and fix impact.

faq.question: Which ecosystems does this skill cover?
faq.answer: The examples cover npm, Python, Go, and Rust dependency scanning.

faq.question: Does the skill change dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: It provides update examples, but its safety guidance requires approval before running automatic fixes.

faq.question: Can it generate an SBOM?
faq.answer: It includes CycloneDX-style generation logic, but the example lists vulnerable components rather than every installed dependency.

faq.question: Does it replace security review?
faq.answer: No. Scanner findings require validation against application exposure, advisory quality, and upgrade impact.

faq.question: Can it run without network access?
faq.answer: Some local analysis may work, but vulnerability databases and tool installation commonly require network access.

faq.question: How should CI handle scanner failures?
faq.answer: CI should distinguish execution errors from clean results, preserve reports, and fail when required evidence is missing.
